name: Kenaf plot on BRIS coastal sands
region: Beach Ridges Interspersed with Swales (BRIS), Kelantan coast
headline: Sand that holds almost no water or nutrients, flooded by the northeast monsoon, then parched by March.
story: A 2 ha plot on the BRIS sands of the Kelantan coast, planted to kenaf for the LKTN buy-back scheme once a year after the northeast monsoon floods recede, then left fallow. The sand holds little water, so a dry spell in March-April hurts, and root-knot nematode thrives. Yields of 6-8 t/ha of stems give a thin margin.

soil_overrides.note: SoilGrids blends the narrow BRIS sand ridges with the clayey swales between them at 250 m. The field sits on a sand ridge mapped as Rudua series by the DOA soil survey, so sand values replace the model estimate.

baseline_rotation.name: Kenaf, then fallow
baseline_rotation.note: Sentinel-2 shows one crop cycle a year; kenaf is the LKTN crop promoted on BRIS soils in Kelantan.

water_context.in_situ_source: JPS tube wells, Kelantan coastal plain
water_context.note: The shallow sand aquifer refills every monsoon but is easily polluted by nitrate and can turn saline near the coast if over-pumped.

kenaf.note: LKTN (National Kenaf and Tobacco Board) buys stems back at a contracted price.

watermelon.note: Kelantan is a major watermelon area; collectors come to the farm.

groundnut.note: Local roasters and snack makers in Kota Bharu.

sweet_potato.note: Pasar besar Kota Bharu and processors.

cassava.note: No starch mill nearby; only the fresh-food market.
